extracted.intended_audience: military and civil engineers, architects, and builders (ancient/technical readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Design and construction guidance for fortifications, siegecraft, bridges, theatres, lifting gear, and related mechanics; practical prescriptions for making walls, towers, signaling, hoists, wheels, and concealed storage. Ancient-technical instructional excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triplex munitione (threefold defence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibemus tribus scilicet; aqua, fossa; muro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defence formed by three elements (water, ditch, wall) makes access difficult. If you make the triple line, the place is not only impregnable but drives attackers to despair. Design defences so attackers cannot easily descend/ascend; provide depth and multiplicity so that if triple-formed it becomes nearly inexpugnable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wall profiles, thickness and internal support
rubrics_metrics.description: Muri enim simplices in singula brachia ... mediocres autem ... Altitudo illius passus centum:nam decem sub fossa, L x. ad summa fosse, xxx. autem supra; aggere interius crassissimo fulciatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify single-wall and thicker-wall dimensions, build foundations and inner fill (agger) strongly. Projected foundations and massive inner supports (very thick backing) are needed; foundation should protrude and if the wall is laid on it, cut the wall so the foundation behaves like a retaining pluteus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tower spacing and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Repulsa constat aggeribus ac turribus in singulos c c. pedes, muro in medio recto, sed superiorius in urbem inclinato.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place towers at regular intervals (given here as every 200 feet) with the wall between them straight and the upper parts leaning toward the city; rounded summits and properly spaced towers prevent siege engines from easily overthrowing defenders. Interior channels and parapets in towers protect defenders and hide approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounded towers and arches (fornicum) stronger
rubrics_metrics.description: Fornicum ratio sic constavit rotundior est; eo firmior usque ad perfecti circuli figuram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rounded (circular) forms — towers and arches tending toward the perfect circle — are firmer. Build vaults/archworks with rounder geometry to gain structural strength up to a perfect circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide internal passageways and canals inside walls
rubrics_metrics.description: In interior parte canalis; per que tuto ire possint custodes. Terra quoque in imo cauata, ut sonent ictus cuniculos suffodientesque, et milites securi circumambulabunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hollow out internal channels and passages within the wall so guards can move safely, inspect, and dig counter-tunnels; include rooms and walks to enable secure circulation and defense operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations should project and engage the wall
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamentum prominet, & si muro insisiat, exciditur mutus ut plutei instar fundamentum forn icis suscipiat ac retineat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make foundations that project and are cut to receive the wall like a pluteus so that the wall is held and retained by the foundation form; ensure firm seating between foundation and superstructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep houses and buildings behind wall line (no projections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ipsa domorum urbis muri alio, ut dixi; muro circumdepbatur ac muniantur, nullaque domus promineat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow houses to project beyond the line of the city wall; keep domestic constructions within the defended polygon so that they do not provide footholds for attackers or obstruct defenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of internal privies, cloacae and pits for utility and defence
rubrics_metrics.description: In singulos centum passus stercoraria cloacae puteaque: nam aquae necessitas abscendere cogit milites, & utilitas adversus ... Stercus aerem corrumpit. Vix vero plures ex muris occulte ad intima cimiteriis multa arcent incommodia; commodumque militibus defend entibus ingens afferunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide privies, sewers and pits within the defended circuit for sanitation, storage and service. Although dung will corrupt air, these features supply utilities, concealment, and amenities useful to troops and defenders; locate them thoughtfully to avoid giving attackers access yet serve garrison needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concealed approaches, secret ways and avoiding easy interception
rubrics_metrics.description: Haec habeat septem passus scaturientis aqua: quonia quod nascitur intercipi, nec tolli ulla arte potest. Dum vero affisset ingredientes mergit: quos non mergit lubrico pede facto & graves aqua prohibet ab ascensu: prohibet & cuniculos ut vix effodi possint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design approaches and ditches to become impassable when filled with liquid or oiled surfaces, making digging of tunnels very difficult. Use wet or lubricated ground to prevent enemy infiltration and undermining of walls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent attackers from extinguishing fires or inserting fire into walls
rubrics_metrics.description: Accedit quod iniecta dissipat ac dissolvit: prohibetque ne ignis injectus eraffetur in murorum perniciem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measures that prevent enemies from setting fire to or otherwise destroying walls (e.g., forms that dissipate thrown combustibles); design surfaces and materials to avoid vulnerability to incendiary attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal communications by torches and prewritten signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sicut: singula faces ardentes collocentur, singulique qui exstant; verba quae significantur sint scripta ante se habeat, & ut lettera succedet quae ad facem pertineat sua; aut duae, tresve, eam eave facem elevando; aut deprimendo; aur in dextra vel sinistra flectendo significet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When communicating across besieged areas, use torch-signals at specific towers and prewritten messages kept ready. Signals may be made by raising/lowering torches or by moving them right/left; ensure correspondences (letters/words mapped to specific torches or motions) are prearranged so allied forces understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer signals over open letters during siege
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedium, quod tutum est; & semper paratum: nec minus licet intelligere quae velint; quia auxilio veniunt aut venturi sunt, quam urbis statum patefacere; paramq differat ab epistola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In besieged situations communicate by signals which are safer and can be prearranged; avoid sending letters that expose the city's state and plans to interception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wall height tradeoffs: high walls vs low walls
rubrics_metrics.description: Sed ad urbis munitione redeo: que si muris altis constabio praeter sumptus maximos in extruendo id habet incommodi, quod ubi vi tormentorum muri deciderint, commodissimum actutissimum pontem hostibus praebebunt. Humiliores vero usui curiores adversus extructus ab oppugnatoribus aggeres neque domus neque milites tutos praebent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High walls are costly and when toppled by siege machines may create bridges for attackers; low walls are less likely to provide such ready crossings but may neither protect houses nor soldiers as effectively. Choose wall height considering expense, vulnerability to falling debris, and defender shelter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct walls so failure is progressive not catastrophic
rubrics_metrics.description: Nam compages illa cum iam sustineatur aliquid habet quo maneat; id ante ruinam frangi necesse est: dum frangitur, ilrepitus fit: ob id quibusdam unicus in aliis plures in quibusdam multo ante; statim in aliis fiunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build wall assemblies with interlocked courses and partial supports so that when damaged they fail progressively rather than wholly at once. Use connecting elements so some portions remain after partial rupture, giving defenders time to respond and preventing immediate catastrophic collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridges: paired beams, spacing and cross-ties to resist river current
rubrics_metrics.description: Tigna bina ... inde praecuta ab imo machinationibus immissa fistic (firmata) ad fluminis naturam prona ex uno latere figes; sic ut tignorum alterum ripa proximus fit. Totidem aequalia ... coniuncta quadruaginta pedum intervallo in inferiori fluminis parte adversus illius impetum prona definigito vocentur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct pontoon/beam bridges using paired main beams anchored on each bank, joined by crossbeams and fibulae (connectors), placed at intervals (here cited 40 feet) with many ties to withstand the river's current; separate upper and lower parts so the upstream portion takes the brunt of the flow and transmits forces across the structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre/amphitheatre geometry and movable scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ponantur igitur semicirculi duo ... partibus ex quibus tota diametros est 120 ... ut Vitruvius docet; qua arte fieri possit ut immota scena ambo theatra in unum coeant amphitheatrum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design theatre semicircles and scenae with precise proportional diameters so that two semicircles can be combined without obstruction; ensure the scena does not permanently impede the amphitheatre's fusion — proportions of arcs and radii must be calculated (numerical relations are given) so circumferences do not conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochlea (screw/pulley) mechanical advantage principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Igitur ex uno pondus trahitur, & quia sustinetur ab s G n x, non erit nisi quarta pars ponderis A, quae 4 singulis funibus sustinetur, quare a quarta parte roboris ferrum trahi poterit. Et si in singulis trochleis tres essent orbiculi; a sexta roboris poterit trahi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase the number of pulleys/screws (orbiculi/spirals) to multiply mechanical advantage: more sheaves reduce the effective load per line. However, more spirals make lifting easier but slower; the proportions and number of turns determine the force reduction (examples quantify how fractions of the original load are borne).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-off: mechanical easing vs speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Sed quia temporum proportio est, ut potentiarum per binos orbiculos; quadruplo per ternos, sexuplo lenius trahet; quam si eodem robore; imò etiam paulo melius supra existens unica traheret fune; longé autem lentius sexuplo vel quadruplo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that increasing mechanical advantage (more pulley rolls/spirals) reduces force required but slows motion proportionally; design machines balancing lifting ease against required speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axle length and multiple axes distribute effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Diximus de axibus ergatarum, quod longiores esse debeant, nam iuxta longitudinis rationem singula capita minuunt pondus. Duplicatiigitur ad dimidium etiam deducunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use longer axles and multiple axes to diminish the load per person: distributing forces across several axles and longer radii reduces the human power needed; examples show how adding axles proportionally increases carrying capacity while reducing per-axle burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wheel size, number and terrain considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Quicumque igitur rotis maioribus innituntur in molli solo facillimé ac celerimé moventur, quod harenam lutum rotarum minimam occupet partem; ... Quamobrem imperatores Romani effeso, id est, curru duarum magnarum rotarum vehebantur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer larger wheels on soft/muddy ground since they displace less mud proportionally and travel faster; fewer larger wheels are often faster than many small ones. Choose wheel size and wheel count relative to terrain and desired speed/capacity, balancing stability and ease of motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use oil and certain vegetable preparations on iron/axles
rubrics_metrics.description: Nam oleum ad motum iuvat ob lenitatem, ... ex materia olei, qualis est foenugrecum. Narrat Josephus ... decocto chalybi foenugreci consperfum pontem adeo labilem reddidisse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lubricate iron and moving parts with oil (e.g., fenugreek-infused) to facilitate motion, reduce friction and retard rust; in cases, vegetable coatings can make wood/iron slippery and impair traction—use with judgment depending on desired effect (ease of motion vs grip).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design concealed storage and secret compartments
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut neque vestigium loci appareat, nec si sciant, nisi constrata pecunia, aut gemmae extrahi. Tabula cauitati obducitur ita arte, ut rima non appareat. In fructu quod amoveri potest cochlea parva e metallo & semina includitur, eiusque clauus superponitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To conceal valuables, build hollowed boards, false bottoms and covert cavities inaccessible without knowledge: use very thin openings externally, false nails, nested small screw-like cavities, metal plates with internal hollows, and bracteae to hide seams. Fill cavities with soft material to mute sound and avoid revealing location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer stable, universal measures and note regional variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Pódus enim certa prae supponit mensuram; mensura vero omnis alicuius necessario est mensura. ... In Italia non ubique eiusdem ponderis aut mensurae; & in singulis mutantur annos. ... Si igitur centesima altitudinis certae pyramidis aut latitudinis pro firma mensura quis statu at, constare poterit apud omnes gentes, & per multa saecula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measures that are durable and as universal as possible (e.g., monuments, pyramids, fixed standards) because local measures, human sizes and material dimensions vary with place and time. When establishing standards, prefer stable references (stone monuments, coin sizes) rather than variable body measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gearing and wheel-to-wheel ratios increase impulse
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoties igitur AB continetur in A3 C; toties in una conversio rota maioris que vocetur H, parna rota DEF circumverterbitur. Igitur qualis proportio magnitudinis ambitus G vel axis ad ambitûm C talis erit numeri revolutionum C ad revolutiones H: igitur C maximo impetu circumcapietur, quia in brevissimo temporis spatio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange large-to-small wheel (gear) ratios so that smaller wheels driven by larger ones achieve high rotational speed and force. Repeated gear reductions/multiplications amplify impulse and were used in siege machines and torsion engines; use toothed rims and successive wheel trains to obtain the desired velocity or torque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material selection: texture, weave and composition matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Sic in naturali; ita his qui arte constant; quos texuntur, & qua in textura admittuntur, tenditatis metas proprias subeunt. Bernucium vocatur. Ergo rennitas in omnibus naturae operibus elegantior non solum sed & roboris ac soliditatis parens est.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose materials with appropriate texture and weave for the task: fine, closely woven textiles or well-textured assemblies can be both elegant and strong. Nature’s models should be emulated where the combination of thinness, strength and lustre yields durable, economical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assuming perpetual motion in machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Videndum an detur inter artificia motus perpetuus. ... Necesse est igitur quod quod fertur, cum in fine est; denuo referatur, si motus debet esse perpetuus. At referri non potest nisi ab excessu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not design or assume a machine with perpetual motion without an external supply or feedback; any apparent perpetual motion must ultimately be referred back to an external cause or a transfer/return of force. Treat cyclical machines with careful accounting of inputs and losses.
